BiblicalUsage: The word is steeped juice, the liquor of grapes, and it appears once, in the law of the Nazarite: he shall drink no liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes or dried, for all the days of his separation.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the grape juice is the test of the vow: the Nazarite gives up even the harmless fruit, because separation means separation, not moderation.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
